meta.title: Use of Reflux Condenser Assembly in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To perform hot continuous extraction of phytochemicals from plant materials under reflux conditions, ensuring complete extraction of thermostable compounds without solvent loss.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for hot extraction of alkaloids, glycosides, tannins, and other thermostable phytochemicals from crude drugs where simple maceration is insufficient.
procedure: Assemble the reflux apparatus: place a round-bottom flask (250 mL or 500 mL) on a heating mantle or water bath; mount a Liebig condenser vertically above the flask using a clamp and retort stand.
Connect rubber tubing from the laboratory cold water supply to the lower inlet of the condenser jacket; connect outlet from the upper port to the sink drain.
Check all glass joints are clean and fit firmly — use a light application of Vaseline only if required for completely sealed operation.
Add the powdered or coarsely powdered drug material into the round-bottom flask.
Add the extraction solvent (typically 6–10× the weight of drug material): ethanol, methanol, water, or hydroalcoholic mixture as per requirement.
Turn on the cooling water supply to the condenser — confirm steady flow before heating.
Begin heating using the heating mantle or water bath — start at low heat and increase gradually.
As the solvent begins to boil, vapours rise, condense in the Liebig condenser, and drip back into the flask — this is reflux.
Maintain gentle reflux (solvent dripping back at 1–2 drops per second) for the required time: typically 1–3 hours.
Monitor the condenser — if vapours escape from the top, increase cooling water flow.
After the reflux period, allow the flask to cool to 60°C before stopping the cooling water.
Filter the warm extract through Whatman No. 1 filter paper in a Buchner funnel.
Collect the filtrate in a clean, labelled beaker; optionally reflux the marc (residue) with fresh solvent for a second extraction.
Concentrate the extract if required using a rotary vacuum evaporator.
Record: drug name, part used, solvent system, solvent volume, reflux time, temperature, and extract yield.
precautions: Always start cooling water BEFORE heating begins — failure to do so allows solvent vapours to escape.
Never heat a completely sealed apparatus — pressure buildup causes explosion.
Use boiling chips (anti-bumping granules) to ensure smooth, even boiling and prevent bumping.
Ensure all glass joints are secure but not over-tightened — thermal expansion can crack tight joints.
Work in a fume hood for volatile and flammable organic solvents (methanol, ethanol, petroleum ether).
Do not add organic solvents to an already-hot flask — add solvents at room temperature before heating.
If a crack is noticed in the round-bottom flask during reflux, immediately reduce heat and discontinue.
